objective: Proof: for any set of allowed states, c lies between a and b in the differ count (d(a,b) = d(a,c) + d(c,b)) iff no state has a = b != c; a not-all-equal knot abc holds iff the three differ counts sum to twice the number of states; hence the differ table determines every nonempty not-all-equal relation on n >= 4 distinctions, fails at n = 3 (one knot against none), and no pairwise count sees a parity knot. Exhaustive code check at n <= 6.
status: Proved 2026-11-17 (refereed R1, confirmed; statement 3(b) proved for every n >= 4): betweenness in the disagreement count iff no state has a = b != c (a knot where its pairs are free); a not-all-equal knot is the count sum 2N; the table determines every nonempty not-all-equal base from four distinctions (with N, every base of complement-closed constraints on at most three places), fails at three; parity invisible to pairs; a chain of m distinctions allows at most 2m joint values; on knot trees tau = steps apart, which determines the base. Slip 'four' corrected to 'six'; statement 5's knot clause scoped to both kinds of threshold.
title: A knot is a betweenness: the differ count determines every not-all-equal base
